items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: The name 'Neely' is mentioned only by the interviewer in a question ('I am, Neely'). The interviewee does not mention Neely, nor does he respond to the name or confirm any relationship with him.

ctx.x: Did any other clarinet players do that besides you? None of them ain't never seen it down there. They ain't gonna do it. That's the way I feel about it. They ain't never played low register till I started putting their hold it on the record, got it, and most of them use it. Those men would all of this hit it and go, but they wouldn't get on in it. They'd just catch a little redstone, play in it, half wind low, half sound.
Well I guess you're about the strongest clarinet player they have left, I am, Neely. Who in the old days was strong like that? Big tone.

Well, what I could say, I liked Pills. He was a pretty good clarinet player. I liked Pills very well. Now Jim was a good clarinet player. Jimbo, you understand? But Jimbo had a whole lot of chicken in him. Yeah. He was ready to run in to see somebody got noise, he couldn't fly. He'd done a couple of times, I'd run him off the truck just by going around him. Just by going there and looking at him playing. Got off the truck, got a man, take a walk. And they saw him home, took one day, went home, got my clarinet,…
